what: DECODE-THREADS (2026-10-26): the C BCIRQ8 decoder computes a large matvec's columns and its packed head's rows in parts on a runner the caller lends -- every matvec kernel over a range of its columns, each output by one part with its chain the whole call's -- so every token and logit is the same at every thread count; the records of the commits that made it (ef6717a, 0c24748 and ea6fc46 against 4bac89e). In one binary, lent the trainer's pool, a token of a synthetic decoder at TinyLlama-1.1B's widths takes x0.473 of its one-thread time at four threads under clang (107.1 -> 51.5 ms) and x0.580 under GCC, x0.458 and x0.498 capped at AVX2; one 1,024 wide x0.585 (x0.731), 512 wide x0.775 (x1.007) and 256 wide x0.962 (x1.169). The 860K decoder's operations are all under the default thresholds, so it splits none and its token keeps its time (x0.971-1.026 at two to four threads). This host is the session's second, a Xeon at 2.80 GHz with 1 MiB of L2 a core and 33 MiB of L3; on its first, where the thresholds were calibrated, the same records of 0c24748 read x0.370 at TinyLlama's widths (x0.351 under GCC). A whole call runs each vector kernel's whole-call instance, Q8-PAIR's the kernel before the ranges instruction for instruction: in one binary holding the three trees' kernel units, every function on a 64-byte boundary, the whole calls of DECODE-THREADS as first committed (ef6717a) took x1.102-1.250 of the tree before's time under clang AVX-512, the tree after's x0.961-1.002, none resolved slower in any build. Under callgrind the qualification, which lends its decoders no runner, takes 135,617,235 -> 135,438,771 instructions on its GEM request, its logits the same.
